methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For a universal closed length-28 word with an 8-step all-ones arc, split the two multiplicity-2 turn-off orders. In the order where the later arc source turns off first, prove that three body slices are difference bases of F_2^6 and that the arc's forced flags have pairwise sums of size at most 16.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one new priced connector operation. This package keeps the published singleton alphabet and answers the length-28 all-ones split requested by the 2026-11-11 eight-source handoff. It does not add a call or change kappa.
bottleneck_link: A universal length-28 singleton word would show the #5234 floor is sharp and could lower the eight-source query bill. The case-II sumset obligation is a necessary condition on one of the two turn-off orders inside an 8-step all-ones interval. No supplier bill is computed, and the condition does not yet exclude that order.
stop_rule: Stop once the turn-off split, the direct-sum flag bound of 16, and one rank-feasible witness in each case for every label pair are checked. Do not search the remaining complement orderings, and do not treat the gap from 16 to 64 as nonexistence.
evidence: Written normalization, flip schedule, and case split. The forced flags of every label pair have direct pairwise sums, and every positive integer solution of x+y+z=9 has pairwise products at most 16. The verifier checks all 40320 coordinate relabelings, the 28-row flag table, walks all 10640 three-pass insertion indices, keeps the lexicographically first rank-feasible witness in each turn-off case for every label pair, checks the length-32 Gray all-ones distance 16, and rejects mutations.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does any case-II complement put enough extra body states into the three slices to make all three pairwise sums equal F_2^6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A no answer would remove one of the two turn-off orders from the length-28 all-ones distance-8 family. The forced flags reach at most 16 sums, while the slices need 64.
open_questions.first_step: For labels (6,7), where one slice already contains the full 6-bit initial-segment flag, list the positive size triples inside the 28-prefix budget whose products are at least 64 and test only walks that realize those sizes.
open_questions.blocked_by: The legal complement orderings are still too many for an unpruned listing. A partial or heuristic search would not be an exclusion.

open_questions.question: Does case I, in which quadrant (0,1) is nonempty, contain a universal length-28 word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The three-sumset reduction uses the empty quadrant, so it does not apply to this order. The inherited gap remains 28 <= f(8) <= 32 until both orders are decided.
open_questions.first_step: Write the two-sumset union that replaces each cross condition when both (0,1) and (1,0) occur.
open_questions.blocked_by: That union is a weaker condition than a single sumset, and no universal length-28 word is known.

open_questions.question: Do the all-ones distances 10, 12, and 14 have a turn-off split with an analogous forced-flag bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The handoff leaves those three anchors unresolved. Distance 8 is the only length whose short arc is a permutation.
open_questions.first_step: For distance 10, record that the short arc uses one source three times and the other seven once, then split on where the two multiplicity-2 sources sit.
open_questions.blocked_by: The identity permutation normalization and the nine-prefix flag decomposition both stop applying once a source repeats inside the arc.

claim_type: scoped written proof with finite exact corroboration
unrun_obligations: No replay of the cited f(7)=24 proof.
No completed search of case-II complement orderings beyond the three-pass insertion witnesses.
No claim that a universal length-28 word does not exist.
No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, supplier admission, or kappa change.
